summary: On a German student visa you may work up to 120 full days or 240 half days per year. The two main models are Minijob (up to €538/month, no income tax) and Werkstudent (higher earnings, partial social insurance). UCB has a Career & Study Orientation office — that is your first stop on campus. A2/B1 German significantly widens what is available to you in Rhineland-Palatinate.

concepts.title: 120 Full Days / 240 Half Days
concepts.body: These are your annual work allowances on a German student visa. Exceeding them violates your visa conditions. Track days carefully — your employer reports hours to the tax authority.

concepts.title: Minijob (Geringfügige Beschäftigung)
concepts.body: Earnings up to €538/month. Employer pays flat-rate social contributions; you pay no income tax. Good for low-commitment work alongside studying. Register through the Minijob-Zentrale.

concepts.title: Werkstudent
concepts.body: For students earning more than €538/month. Subject to partial social insurance contributions. Requires that studying remains your primary activity — max 20 hours per week during semester.

concepts.title: Language Opens Doors
concepts.body: Most local employers in Birkenfeld and Rhineland-Palatinate require at least A2 German for practical roles. Sustainability and engineering companies near campus do hire international Werkstudenten with B1 or higher.
